Congressman Tim Moore Votes to Extend Government Funding, Avert Shutdown | Representative Tim Moore Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Congressman Tim Moore Votes to Extend Government Funding, Avert Shutdown Tuesday, September 1, 2026 WASHINGTON, D.C.  - Today, the U.S. House passed H.R. 6500, the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027, to continue federal funding through December 11, 2026. This legislation prevents a September 30, 2026 government shutdown while allowing Congress to continue working on the full-year FY2027 appropriations bills. "I'm proud to support this clean, straightforward continuing resolution that protects Americans from the costs of a shutdown and ensures election-year politics don't jeopardize the funding process,"  said Congressman Moore. "This short-term measure prevents a last-minute funding crisis, guards the critical services Americans rely on, and preserves the path to completing full-year FY27 appropriations without allowing political games to dictate the process." This legislation continues programs at the funding rates and under the conditions established in the FY2026 appropriations laws. It also preserves funding authority for FEMA disaster relief and continues programs such as WIC, SNAP, flood insurance, small-business lending, and assistance for low-income families. H.R. 6500 now advances to President Trump’s desk to be signed into law. Congressman Tim Moore Introduces Bipartisan HUD Disaster Information Improvement Act | Representative Tim Moore Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Congressman Tim Moore Introduces Bipartisan HUD Disaster Information Improvement Act Thursday, July 30, 2026 WASHINGTON, D.C.  - Today, Congressman Tim Moore (NC-14) introduced H.R. 9992, the HUD Disaster Information Improvement Act, which would facilitate disaster relief information sharing between Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), and Small Business Administration (SBA). This bipartisan legislation is co-led by Congresswoman Brittany Pettersen (D-CO-07).  “In the wake of Hurricane Helene, it became clear that we need better coordination between agencies to get disaster assistance to communities faster,”   said Congressman Tim Moore.  “The GAO and HUD’s Inspector General have identified serious challenges with data sharing, duplication-of-benefits determinations, and improper payments. This legislation strengthens transparency and coordination between agencies, helping reduce waste, fraud, and abuse while ensuring disaster relief gets to folks more efficiently.” “Each year, families across the country face more frequent and more intense severe weather and natural disasters. In Colorado, we recently saw historic fires sweep across the state, destroying homes, communities, and lives. It’s important that we have an all-hands-on deck approach to how we respond to these disasters so communities can rebuild,” said Rep. Brittany Pettersen.  “I am proud to co-lead this bipartisan legislation with Rep. Moore. Our bill lays out a clearer path for how HUD can work seamlessly with FEMA and the SBA to support families and businesses when a disaster strikes. Congressman Tim Moore Announces $7.8 Million in EDA Funding for Hurricane Helene Recovery in Forest City | Representative Tim Moore Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Congressman Tim Moore Announces $7.8 Million in EDA Funding for Hurricane Helene Recovery in Forest City Thursday, September 3, 2026 WASHINGTON, D.C.  - Today, Congressman Tim Moore (NC-14) announced $7.8 million in federal funding from the Economic Development Administration (EDA) for Hurricane Helene recovery in Forest City, North Carolina. This EDA investment is estimated to create 28 new jobs and generate over $9 million in private investment. “While our communities in Western North Carolina have made significant progress since Hurricane Helene, there is still important work ahead,”  said Congressman Moore.   “This funding will help Forest City build the infrastructure necessary to support economic development and create new jobs. I appreciate President Trump and the EDA for supporting Western North Carolina’s recovery and helping our communities come back stronger.”   $7,798,480 will go to the Town of Forest City, North Carolina for the construction of a new electric substation to support economic development and resilience to address economic distress caused by Hurricane Helene. Congressman Tim Moore Announces $3.8 Million in FEMA Funding for Hurricane Helene Recovery Projects in Lake Lure, Chimney Rock, and Polk County | Representative Tim Moore Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Congressman Tim Moore Announces $3.8 Million in FEMA Funding for Hurricane Helene Recovery Projects in Lake Lure, Chimney Rock, and Polk County Thursday, August 27, 2026 WASHINGTON, D.C.  - Today, Congressman Tim Moore (NC-14) announced $3.8 million in federal funding from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) for Hurricane Helene recovery across Lake Lure, Chimney Rock, and Polk County. Projects include critical sewer repairs, dam restoration, and public assistance. “While it has been nearly two years since Hurricane Helene devastated our communities, significant recovery work remains,”  said Congressman Moore. “This additional funding will help restore necessary infrastructure across Lake Lure, Chimney Rock, and Polk County. I appreciate President Trump, Secretary Mullin, and the folks at FEMA for continuing to prioritize Western North Carolina's recovery.” $1,810,198.80 will go to the Town of Lake Lure for permanent repairs to the sewer collection system following severe damage from Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 406 of the Robert T. Stafford Act. $1,555,804.86 will go to the Town of Lake Lure for permanent repairs to the Lake Lure Dam following Hurricane Helene. The repairs include removing and replacing concrete stairs, chain link fence, dam barrel, traffic signs, crossing sign, and embankment restoration. This funding is authorized under Section 406 of the Robert T. Stafford Act. $312,717.28 will go to Chimney Rock Village to support management of Public Assistance grants as a result of Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 324 of the Robert T. Stafford Act. $142,298.10 will go to Polk County to support the earthen retention dam and related repairs or replacements following the damage from Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 406 of the Robert T. Stafford Act. Media Press Releases Press Kit Washington DC Office 1424 Longworth House O

Res. 113, the Budget Resolution. This legislation safeguards elections, supports troops, and strengthens America’s food supply. “Americans overwhelmingly support voter ID, yet not every state has enacted strong election integrity laws like North Carolina,"   said Congressman Moore. “This resolution outlines a framework to finally secure our elections, deliver critical assistance to American farmers, and strengthen our national defense. It advances reforms like voter ID across all fifty states, giving Americans confidence that their elections are secure, and provides supplemental funding to ensure baseline military readiness and strengthen American Agriculture.”   Watch Congressman Moore’s floor speech  here . H. Con. Res. 113 now advances to the Senate. Congressman Tim Moore Introduces Resolution Honoring Shelby as Permanent Home of American Legion World Series, Recognizing 100 Years | Representative Tim Moore Skip to main content Newsletter Subscribe | Accessibility Congressman Tim Moore Introduces Resolution Honoring Shelby as Permanent Home of American Legion World Series, Recognizing 100 Years Friday, August 14, 2026 WASHINGTON, D.C.  - Yesterday, Congressman Tim Moore (NC-14) introduced H.Res. 1482, the American Legion World Series Resolution, which recognizes 100 years of American Legion Baseball and the American Legion World Series and honors Shelby, North Carolina for serving as the permanent home of the American Legion World Series. “Since 2011, the American Legion World Series has been a welcomed tradition in Shelby and across Cleveland County,”  said Congressman Tim Moore.   “As we celebrate 100 years of American Legion Baseball, this milestone reminds us of the lasting impact this event has both on and off the field. It teaches young athletes the value of hard work, sportsmanship, and patriotism. I’m grateful to the volunteers, coaches, and families who make this event such a source of pride for our community and continue to honor the legacy of our veterans.” The 2026 American Legion World Series, held August 13 through August 18, 2026 at Veterans Field in Shelby, marks the 100th anniversary of the first American Legion World Series, a milestone reflecting a century of service to American communities and to the young athletes who have worn the American Legion uniform. Read the full text of the resolution  HERE . "This funding will help Rutherford and Mecklenburg Counties address properties at risk of future flooding and landslides and better protect against future storms . I appreciate President Trump, Secretary Mullin, and the folks at FEMA for continuing to prioritize Western North Carolina's recovery.” $10,638,923.44 will go to Rutherford County to fund the acquisition and demolition of 23 properties impacted by Hurricane Helene. The acquired properties will be returned to green space and deed restricted to reduce the risk of future damage from flooding and landslides. This funding is authorized under Section 404 of the Robert T. Stafford Act. $400,000 will go to Rutherford County to support management costs associated with the acquisition and demolition of 23 properties impacted by Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 324 of the Robert T. Stafford Act. $6,651,850.69 will go to Mecklenburg County to fund the acquisition and demolition of 19 properties impacted by Hurricane Helene. This funding is authorized under Section 404 of the Robert T.
